titleEn: One Step Out from Behind the Door!

pages.text: "Mom, a boat I don't know is here!" Pongi looked through the window at the winter waterfront. A boat she had never seen was tied to the post outside. A duck waddled toward their house.
Knock, knock! Mom, wearing her headscarf, opened the door. "I'm the duck who moved in next door. Hello!" said the duck. Pongi felt shy and quickly hid behind the door.
Behind the door, Pongi's heart thumped. Only her red neck cord peeked through the gap. "I... I'm too shy to come out," she said softly, squeezing her eyes shut.
Mom slipped behind the door and crouched beside Pongi. "You feel shy? I felt that way when I first came to this village too. You don't have to do everything. Let's start with something very small."
"Want to try whispering it in my ear first?" Mom leaned closer. Pongi whispered a tiny "Hello..." into her ear. "Wow, well done! One step out from behind the door!" Mom smiled wide.
"Now just one step out from behind the door." Mom held Pongi's paw. Pongi took one step forward. Oh! The duck was smiling. Pongi's mouth slowly turned up.
Pongi stood in front of the duck, with Mom right beside her. A big breath, then, "Hello! I'm Pongi!" Her voice was very quiet, but she said her name too. She thumped her tail!
The duck bowed a little in greeting. Mom clapped her paws. Pongi lifted her shoulders and smiled wide. "I... I did it!" she called.
Pongi counted three steps at the doorway. "One, say you feel shy! Two, try it quietly with Mom first! Three, take one step out!" Mom smiled beside her.
Mom gave Pongi a snug hug. "You said hello first, Pongi!" Even when she feels shy, one little step at a time can help her say hello. Pongi grinned and called, "One step out from behind the door!"
